Title: Private files can be downloaded by unrelated signed-in users
Actual result: The free learner receives HTTP 200 and the exact private file bytes. The course API correctly returns 403 to the same learner.
Reproduction: Assigned teacher uploads a synthetic private course PDF; a free learner not enrolled in that course requests the returned /uploads URL.
Recommendation: Replace the shared authenticated static-file mount with attachment ownership and purpose checks. Separate deliberately public assets from private submissions, contracts, resumes and onboarding documents.
Acceptance criteria: An owner/assigned staff member can retrieve the attachment; unrelated free/student/recruiter accounts get 403/404 even with its exact URL; unauthenticated access stays denied.

Title: Password reset leaves existing sessions valid
Actual result: Reset succeeds, but the previously issued session still receives HTTP 200. Tokens last seven days and contain no password/session version.
Reproduction: Sign in as qa.free, retain that session, reset its password using the local reset token, and call /api/auth/me with the old cookie.
Recommendation: Version user sessions or maintain revocable server sessions. Rotate/invalidate old sessions on recovery and administrative password reset; give users a revoke-other-sessions action.
Acceptance criteria: After recovery, cookies created before the reset return 401; the new session and password work; reused reset tokens fail.

Title: Saving cleared profile fields retains the old data
Actual result: The UI says Profile saved, but QA Browser City remains. The API filters out blank values before updating the profile.
Reproduction: Edit City to QA Browser City, save, edit again, erase City, and save. Reopen profile and inspect the persisted local user record.
Recommendation: Distinguish omitted fields from explicit clears; allow empty/null values for optional fields and return the canonical saved profile.
Acceptance criteria: Clearing City, Goal and Links removes each stored value and keeps it empty after refresh and a new session; mandatory fields receive specific validation.

Title: Authentication and refresh lose the intended destination
Actual result: Sign-in goes to /dashboard instead of Showcase. Refreshing Settings goes to Overview. Course/task selections share unchanged URLs, preventing reliable links.
Reproduction: Open /showcase while signed out, complete the login form, then separately open Settings and refresh the dashboard.
Recommendation: Give significant views stable URLs and preserve a validated same-origin returnTo through login, expiry and logout recovery. Restore the active route on load.
Acceptance criteria: A bookmarked course/task/settings route survives refresh; authentication returns there; Back/Forward retraces navigation; external return URLs are rejected.

Title: Unsubmitted code is lost on task switches and refresh
Page / component: Free course and paid task workspaces
Actual result: Free task switching recreates an empty editor. Refresh returns free users to the catalogue and paid users to Overview. No draft warning was shown. Submitted paid code does reload when the task is reopened.
Reproduction: Type code without submitting. Switch from task 1 to task 2 and back on the free course, or refresh a free/paid task.
Recommendation: Autosave drafts per user/course/task/language, show save state, restore before rendering the editor, and warn when leaving work that has not been saved. Preserve the latest successful submission separately.
Acceptance criteria: Desktop and 390px mobile drafts survive task switching, Back/Forward, refresh, session expiry and sign-in; another account never inherits them. An interrupted save has a visible recovery path.
Evidence: evidence/browser-workflows.json — DRAFT-SWITCH/REFRESH; evidence/final-browser-checks.json — PAID-DRAFT-REFRESH; evidence/annotated-draft-loss-desktop.png; public/js/open.js:1361; public/js/dashboard.js:4853

Title: A teacher can certify a student outside their course
Actual result: HTTP 200 creates a certificate. The public verification page describes the nonmember as having completed the course and lists its concepts.
Reproduction: An assigned teacher issues a course certificate using the ID of QA Empty Student, who has no enrollment in that batch.
Recommendation: Validate enrollment and the configured completion rule before course certification. Keep any exceptional administrative issuance as a separate permission with a recorded reason.
Acceptance criteria: An instructor cannot issue a course certificate to a nonmember or ineligible learner. Valid graduates can be certified once, and verification reflects the recorded completion basis.
Evidence: evidence/operations-initial.json — CERT-NONMEMBER; evidence/final-browser-checks.json — CERT-VERIFY-UI; evidence/certificate-verification.png; server.js:2778-2806

Title: Several failed data requests leave permanent loading screens
Page / component: Assignments / Talent Profile / Hiring Interest / teacher list
Actual result: Assignments remains Loading. Talent Profile and Hiring Interest also remain Loading after real local 503 responses. The role survey captured unhandled errors.
Reproduction: Return a deliberate HTTP 503 for /api/my/quests and open Assignments. Also open student Talent Profile/Hiring Interest with PostgreSQL unavailable.
Recommendation: Use a shared loading/error/empty/success state component. Catch render errors, retain existing content when possible, provide retry, and explain temporary feature unavailability in learner language.
Acceptance criteria: A failed, aborted or timed-out request removes the loader, announces a useful error and exposes Retry; a successful retry restores the screen without a full reload.
Evidence: evidence/browser-workflows.json — ERROR-ASSIGNMENTS; evidence/browser-survey.json — view-student-talent-profile, view-student-hiring-interest; evidence/annotated-loading-error.png; public/js/dashboard.js:1327,2816,3133

Title: Challan is marked sent even when no email was sent
Actual result: HTTP 200 advances the registration to challan_sent although the mail provider skips delivery. The route calls markSent without awaiting a delivery outcome.
Reproduction: Generate a synthetic challan with SMTP disabled, then use the challan send endpoint. Inspect its registration stage.
Recommendation: Track queued, provider-accepted and failed mail states. Advance the workflow only at the documented successful handoff; retain retry and a downloadable PDF. Repeated send attempts need deduplication.
Acceptance criteria: Disabled SMTP, provider rejection and network failure cannot produce a Sent status. A test-provider acknowledgement advances the correct record exactly once.

Title: Repeated course registration creates duplicate records
Actual result: Both requests return 200 and two distinct registrations appear for the same learner/course. Newsletter and event duplication checks behave more safely.
Reproduction: Submit the same name, email and course twice using the normal registration payload.
Recommendation: Define duplicate behavior per learner and offering, use idempotency keys, and show an existing registration receipt when the same request is retried.
Acceptance criteria: Double-click, timeout/retry and resubmission create one active registration per learner/offering, while registration for another course remains allowed.

Title: Unknown course codes are accepted and stored
Actual result: The API reports success and stores a truncated code, DOES-NOT-EXI, which is not an offering. No valid enrollment route can be derived from it.
Reproduction: Submit a registration with course_code DOES-NOT-EXIST. Inspect the resulting record and its available batches.
Recommendation: Resolve the offering server-side, reject missing/unknown codes, and store the authoritative title and price identifier rather than trusting client text.
Acceptance criteria: Unknown/missing/deactivated offerings return a field-level 400 and create no record; valid courses and modeled bundles use authoritative identifiers.

Title: Teachers can award course gems to nonmembers
Actual result: HTTP 200 persists the award for the nonmember and changes their gem total. Validation checks student role but not enrollment.
Reproduction: Assigned teacher awards 25 gems to QA Empty Student, who is not enrolled in the teacher’s batch.
Recommendation: Require recipient enrollment in the authorized batch and record a reason and actor. Keep a separately authorized institute-wide award action if needed.
Acceptance criteria: A teacher’s course award to a nonmember fails and changes no totals; valid awards are persisted and auditable.

Title: Quiz request body can override the authorized batch
Actual result: The server authorizes batch 1 but creates the quiz in batch 2 and returns HTTP 200. req.body overwrites batch_id during object spread.
Reproduction: As a teacher of batch 1, POST to /api/batches/1/quizzes with body batch_id:2, where batch 2 has no assigned teacher.
Recommendation: Whitelist quiz fields and set batch_id exclusively from req.batch after parsing the body. Review analogous route/body ID merges.
Acceptance criteria: A conflicting body ID is rejected or ignored; every created quiz belongs to the URL batch that passed authorization; unauthorized batches are unchanged.

Title: Live course navigation retains the Free-only filter
Actual result: The active navigation changes to Live, but cFree remains free and only free language families appear.
Reproduction: Open /open#free, then select Live Tech Courses in the main navigation.
Recommendation: Make navigation mode and filter state one source of truth. Set or reset applicable filters on both mode changes and show active filters clearly.
Acceptance criteria: Switching between Free and Live consistently shows the advertised offerings; search and tier filters combine predictably and clearing filters restores results.

Title: Coordinator UI exposes actions whose APIs reject that role
Actual result: The survey recorded 403 for /api/instructors-lite and /api/admin/leads; Teachers retains a Loading section and Reports exposes an Admin access only result. Coordinator can also write chat despite read-only documentation.
Failing step: Render authorized actions and recover denied sections
Reproduction: Sign in as coordinator and navigate to Teachers and Reports. Use the visible lead-related affordances.
Recommendation: Define coordinator capabilities explicitly, then share them between API gates and visible navigation. Resolve whether course-chat participation is an intentional exception to read-only access.
Acceptance criteria: Every visible coordinator action has an allowed, scoped endpoint; unavailable actions are omitted/explained; any read-only exception is documented and tested.
Evidence: evidence/browser-survey.json — role-errors-coordinator, view-coordinator-admin-teachers, view-coordinator-admin-analytics; evidence/api-checks.json — SEC-04-coordinator-write

Title: Marketing contradicts current dates, catalogue and gem rules
Actual result: Marketing still promotes a July 31 registration deadline and August cohort; labels say 31 courses and 3 free courses while the catalogue has 39 offerings including 10 free. Landing Glow starts at 100 gems; the actual stage threshold is 250 (Nova 2000 vs 4000).
Reproduction: Compare the September 9 landing page and course catalogue with actual catalogue and stage data.
Recommendation: Drive counts, stage ranges and active cohort dates from the same data as enrollment and progress. Expire campaign urgency copy automatically.
Acceptance criteria: Dates match the active offering; historical campaigns cannot claim seats are filling; counts match catalogue definitions; every stage threshold matches the dashboard.
Evidence: evidence/browser-survey-public.json — landing-desktop, open-desktop; evidence/catalogue-snapshot.json; public/landing.html:426,503-520,624; store.js:31-38

Title: Automatic grading failure has no durable recovery workflow
Actual result: The task is stored ungraded and friendly courses promise grading shortly. No retry worker or manual open-task grading route was found. Resubmission clears score/gems before a replacement grade succeeds.
Reproduction: Submit a valid free task with AI disabled (local fault configuration); inspect response, persistence and processing code. Inspect resubmission of a previously scored task.
Recommendation: Persist a grading job with pending/failed/retrying status and a staff retry path. Keep the previous completed attempt/grade until the replacement is successfully graded.
Acceptance criteria: Provider timeout/rejection can be retried without another upload; learners see a truthful status; successful recovery updates progress once; a failed retry does not erase an earned grade.
Evidence: evidence/api-checks.json — LEARN-05-submit-persist; evidence/browser-workflows.json — SUBMIT-RETRY; server.js:4090-4132; store.js:3955-3964

Title: Advertised course bundle creates a zero-fee challan and cannot enroll
Actual result: A PKR 43,500 advertised bundle generates gross/net PKR 0. Its available_batches is empty and enrollment returns Choose a valid batch for this course. PATH is not resolved as a course or bundle.
Reproduction: Use the advertised PATH registration payload, generate its challan, simulate local Finance clearance, and try Admissions enrollment.
Recommendation: Model bundles as real offerings with component enrollments, authoritative prices and a batch choice for each required course. Until supported, remove the actionable bundle registration offer.
Acceptance criteria: The published PKR 43,500 price reaches the challan; payment clearance lets Admissions place the learner in every component; completion is atomic or explicitly recoverable.
Evidence: evidence/bundle-and-rules.json — BUNDLE-PRICE, BUNDLE-ENROLL; public/js/open.js:506-515,625-650; store.js:2355-2371; server.js:3930-3950

Title: Course progress and certification use different pass rules
Actual result: Backend passed is true with average 93 despite a failed task. The frontend requires each task to meet the pass mark and cannot show all tasks complete. Different places also mention an average, all tasks, and a final exam.
Reproduction: In an isolated business-rule fixture, grade all 15 JavaScript tasks: first 0, remaining 100. Compare backend passed with the UI’s per-task rule.
Recommendation: Choose and document one pass rule, then calculate progress and certificate eligibility on the server from that shared rule. Align all course copy.
Acceptance criteria: Boundary fixtures (one failed task/high average, exactly pass mark, missing grade, regrade) produce identical progress, completion and certificate eligibility across UI/API.

Title: Challenge review corrections can award the same win twice
Actual result: First approval awards 40; rejection leaves those 40; reapproval raises the total to 80. Repeating approval without changing status correctly awards once. The normal UI exposes review buttons only for pending work, so the failing correction sequence is API-level.
Failing step: Reconcile rewards when a review changes
Reproduction: Create a 40-gem challenge and approve its submission. Using the authorized admin review API, reject that approved submission and approve it again.
Recommendation: Use a unique reward identity per challenge and learner. Reject unsupported review transitions or explicitly reconcile the previous award when an authorized correction changes the result.
Acceptance criteria: Approve/repeat/reject/reapprove cannot create two rewards for one win. Any reversal is visible and auditable; the displayed status agrees with earned gems.

Title: Duplicate hackathon teammates receive duplicate prizes
Actual result: The stored team is [4,12,12]. Finalization awards student 12 twice, totalling 60 instead of 30. Repeat finalization is rejected correctly, but duplicated members are not removed.
Failing step: Resolve unique teammates and award each person once
Reproduction: Register a synthetic paid team with qa.empty entered twice in member_regs. Approve its simulated payment, submit, score and finalize a 30-gem first prize.
Recommendation: Resolve teammate identifiers to a unique set of user IDs before validating team size. Enforce one prize per event/place/person and guard legacy duplicate records at finalization.
Acceptance criteria: Repeated username/reg-number aliases create one membership or a clear validation error. Every eligible teammate receives exactly one advertised prize after repeated finalize requests.

Title: Modal keyboard focus escapes into the page
Actual result: The sign-in modal has role=dialog and aria-modal=true, but focus remains on BODY; the first Tab reaches a background link. Escape support and global focus styling already exist.
Recommendation: Move focus into the dialog, keep Tab/Shift+Tab inside, make the background inert and restore focus to its trigger.
Acceptance criteria: Opening, using and closing each dialog is possible with keyboard only; no focus reaches obscured controls.

Title: Mobile discovery requires too much scrolling
Actual result: The 390px all-course page screenshot is 12,156px tall; headers, promotion and course cards create a long route to later offerings. The layout fits horizontally.
Recommendation: Prioritize search and relevant categories, use concise cards, preserve filters and add progressive pagination/load more with a result count.
Acceptance criteria: A learner can find a specific free or paid course without traversing the full catalogue; filter state survives return from course detail.

Title: Recommendation summaries end mid-word
Actual result: Several descriptions visibly end with fragments such as production-se or developer ca; the truncation does not explain that more text is available.
Recommendation: Use line clamping with an ellipsis, concise editorial summaries and a clear course detail affordance.
Acceptance criteria: No summary ends with an unexplained cut word at desktop or mobile widths; full detail is reachable.

Title: Learning terminology and next steps compete
Actual result: The same journey alternates among modules, levels, lessons, lectures, tasks, quests, assignments and final exam. The free course lists a final exam without a distinct tested exam step.
Recommendation: Use a stable hierarchy: Course → Module → Lesson → Task. State the actual completion policy next to progress and identify any final assessment explicitly.
Acceptance criteria: A learner can identify the next required action and all requirements for completion from the curriculum without reconciling contradictory labels.

Title: Integration failures expose developer setup instructions
Actual result: Local unavailable states tell learners to set API keys or configure PostgreSQL. The Talent gallery at least replaces its loader with an error, while dashboard counterparts do not.
Recommendation: Show a user-facing unavailable message and recovery action; put configuration diagnostics in authorized system health/logs.
Acceptance criteria: Student-facing errors contain no environment-variable or infrastructure setup instructions and provide a next step.

Title: Registration has no durable receipt/status destination
Actual result: The success dialog says an email is on its way and asks applicants to wait. The public response has only ok, and no applicant tracking or resume link was observed.
Recommendation: Return a reference and a status page with next steps, contact route, resend status and the selected offering. Keep sensitive payment data protected.
Acceptance criteria: After refresh or a missed email, the applicant can recover their registration status without creating another record.

Title: Mandatory onboarding can obstruct exploration
Page / component: Free/student first contact and staff onboarding
Actual result: Learners without a phone are blocked by a non-dismissable WhatsApp form, including when browsing the open site. The copy combines certificates with promotional communication. This is an observed product choice, not asserted to be a technical failure.
Recommendation: Explain the immediate purpose; permit sign-out and returning later, and separate required account contact from optional promotional preferences.
Acceptance criteria: A new user can understand the requirement, correct an error, sign out or resume later without being trapped behind an overlay.

Title: Small secondary links and dense navigation need touch review
Actual result: Login recovery/signup links measure about 16px high; catalogue footer links about 15px. Primary buttons and responsive single-column forms are usable in the tested viewport.
Recommendation: Increase the padded hit area of secondary actions, group mobile navigation and keep labels readable.
Acceptance criteria: Primary actions have a 44px design target; small secondary links have adequate spacing/padding and can be selected without adjacent activation in touch tests.

Title: Admin status presentation needs clearer operational meaning
Actual result: The overview includes escaped · text and a clipped Operational label in a narrow health card. A dry-run bulk provider is shown as operational even when it is not configured; the detail does disclose dry run.
Recommendation: Use clear Healthy / Disabled / Test mode / Failed labels, wrap diagnostic text and format separators once.
Acceptance criteria: Statuses and details stay readable at 1440px and 390px; a disabled/test integration is visually distinct from an available delivery service.
